title: POC: outage-sim-and-fallback-routing-tuning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on outage simulation results and tuning fallback routing for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Discussed observed p95/p99 latency spikes during simulated egress blackouts, KV cache warmup behavior after failover, and patching plan for kernel update. Agreed on a rehearsed blackout runbook, additional telemetry to capture, and next steps for a second outage sim with canary routing enabled.
action_items: Daniel Mayer (Redwood SE): run scripted outage sim with 10% egress blackhole and gather p95/p99 + CPU/GPU utilization logs; due 2026-10-22
Maya Chen (Stratum CTO): provide service topology and the list of VIPs and egress CIDR ranges used in production; due 2026-10-19
Leah Kim (Redwood CSM): share latest runbook draft and example noise-filter query for traces; due 2026-10-18
Arjun Patel (Stratum Infra): enable access to test VPC peering logs and confirm ability to shadow traffic for canary; due 2026-10-21
next_steps: Schedule full blackout rehearsal w/ SREs and on-call (tentative 2026-10-28)
Redwood to push kernel rollback safepoint and provide rollback checklist
Customer to validate IAM role for telemetry upload to Redwood staging bucket
SE to attach latency trace examples and p95/p99 CSV to the ticket
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood CSM), Maya (Stratum CTO), Arjun (Infra Lead), Priya (Security), Jonas (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Went over the outage sim results from last week's test where we blackholed the egress for one region. Noted increased p99s when fallback routing activated, and slow KV cache warmup causing higher cost and latency for first requests. Discussed kernel/driver upgrade plan and a rehearsal runbook.

00:00:03 Sophie: alright everyone I think we can start, thanks for joining the blackout rehearsal sync. we're on for 54 minutes. quick roll call?
00:00:10 Maya: maya here, arjun and priya and jonas with me, thanks
00:00:13 Daniel: daniel here from redwood se, i ran the sim last thursday and i have the logs
00:00:20 Leah: leah on cs, i'll track action items and runbook updates

00:02:05 Sophie: ok daniel can you walk us through the sim results, like what we saw at p95 and p99, and the fallback path behaviour
00:02:18 Daniel: yeah so we did a staged egress blackhole for 12 minutes on the primary region. first thing, p95 stayed within target roughly, average was fine, but p99 spiked up to 980ms in some tails, and we saw a cluster of retries — some of that was client side retry, but the bigger driver looked like kv cache cold misses after failover. the runtime routed to fallback nodes which are on the dedicated variant and that was fine but the kv cache warming was slower because the request patterns changed and prefix caching didn't hit. so first‑minute requests were like 2–3x slower. also observed an increase in tokenization overhead on the dedicated pool, weirdly, as if the batching behavior changed.
00:03:02 Arjun: so are you saying the fallback nodes are fine but the cache missing is causing the big p99 blips?
00:03:10 Daniel: exactly, fallback routing is working, the model execution was stable, it's the statefulness around kv + prefix caching and the warmup hit rate. also a couple of kernels ran a less-optimal path after the recent runtime switch — i noted some AVX/driver mismatches in logs.
00:04:00 Priya: small note on security, when we switched to fallback the egress path touched a different enclave and we had extra TLS handshakes. that extra handshake time amplified the latency a bit. need to confirm certs are pinned for the fallbacks.
00:04:30 Sophie: good call. daniel, do you have the cert chains and the handshake timing?
00:04:38 Daniel: yes i have a pcap-ish summary and handshake timing in the spreadsheet i uploaded to the ticket, but the transcription maybe garbled — i'll attach the raw traces.
00:06:12 Jonas: one oddity — during the sim our autoscaler kicked in and started shifting traffic, we saw a brief spike in GPU utilization that correlated with a retry storm from a few clients. that made the tail worse.
00:06:30 Daniel: that matches, the client retry policy needs to be a little more backoff-aware during failover. we recommended a jittered exponential backoff in the notes.
00:07:05 Maya: from business side, we need to ensure SLOs survive a 10 minute region outage. the p99 thing worries me. what remedial steps can we take?
00:07:20 Sophie: actionables in short: (1) rehearse a blackout with canary routing enabled, (2) tune the KV caching and pre-warm on failover, (3) telemetry - capture p95/p99 plus TLS handshake metrics and cache hit rates, (4) validate kernel/driver versions across fallback nodes — roll forward or rollback path.
00:07:54 Arjun: on the kernel note — we recently upgraded to kernel 5.18 on the dedicated fleet to get a new nvidia driver, could that be the mismatch?
00:08:06 Daniel: yep it's plausible. some of the vectorized kernels have slightly different codegen and we saw non-fatal perf regressions on 5.18 in a subset of models. not catastrophic but explains the tokenization timing difference. we have a safe rollback plan.
00:09:30 Priya: also need to make sure audit logs contain the routing fallback events explicitly — we need that for compliance. the current audit stream has a generic routing event but not the detailed egress change.
00:09:48 Leah: we can add a structured fallback_event in the audit with fields for original_path, fallback_path, timestamp, and reason. i'll propose a schema and post it.
00:11:10 Daniel: quick demo-ish: i can share a snippet — when we flip to fallback, the runtime emits "route.swap" and then multiple "cache.miss" logs. the misses are concentrated in the first 30–60 seconds. the cache misses were about 42% higher than baseline on our test.
00:11:50 Arjun: ok can we pre-warm? like when the route.swap happens can we prime the KV keys we know are hot?
00:12:05 Daniel: yes — two options: pre-warm via a shadow priming job or do predictive prefetch from the profile that redwood collects. priming is immediate but adds cost; predictive prefetch is smarter but takes a couple of iterations to converge.
00:12:35 Maya: cost is fine for the rehearsal, we want reliability first.
00:13:00 Sophie: good, for the rehearsal we'll enable priming. daniel will run priming in the next sim.
00:13:20 Jonas: on telemetry, i'm going to need a map of metrics we want to ingest into our observability stack. what list do you suggest?
00:13:30 Daniel: p95/p99 latency, token-level timing, cache.hit_ratio, cache.miss_count, route.swap events, tls.handshake_ms, gpu.utilization, kernel.driver_version, and client.retry_count. also trace ids for slow traces.
00:14:10 Priya: and retention of traces for 30 days for compliance please.
00:14:20 Leah: noted. we'll include retention options in the runbook.
00:15:05 Sophie: about canary routing — we want to test canary fallback enabling with maybe 5% traffic before doing full switch. does your infra support shadowing?
00:15:20 Arjun: we can shadow; we prefer not to redirect real traffic until we're confident. 5% canary is doable.
00:15:40 Daniel: we'll run two sims — one with shadow priming and 5% canary, second full blackout rehearsal. the first will measure warmup behavior without affecting users.
00:16:10 Maya: timeline?
00:16:15 Daniel: propose week of 2026-10-26 for the canary, and full blackout w/ SRE week of 2026-10-28 — both in coordination with your on-call.
00:16:40 Sophie: that gives us a little breathing room to patch or rollback kernels. daniel, what's the rollback safepoint look like?
00:16:55 Daniel: it's an automated image flip at the fleet level plus a config gating step. if metrics cross threshold we flip back to previous image within 5 minutes; we also have a manual kill switch. i'll supply the checklist.
00:17:30 Priya: ensure key rotation and KMS access is not broken during rollout — last time we had a rotation that caused auth failures on a canary.
00:17:45 Daniel: noted; will validate KMS permissions.
00:18:55 Arjun: i have a question about the routing policy: when route.swap happens do you prefer a fallback pool with the same quantization profile or a cheaper quantized variant? we care about cost too.
00:19:10 Sophie: good tradeoff. for rehearsals use identical profile to observe pure routing behavior. for production fallback we can test the quantized cheaper variant but only if quality checks pass.
00:19:30 Maya: prod fallback to cheaper variant is ok if we maintain acceptable output quality. can we have auto-quality checks?
00:19:40 Daniel: yes we can run lightweight evals on sampled prompts post-fallback; redwood optimize provides that out of box. we'll set a quality threshold and auto-fallback to the last known-good model if quality drops.
00:20:05 Jonas: regarding the spike we saw, any quick config changes to reduce it without code changes?
00:20:15 Daniel: tune client retry policy to add jitter and increase initial backoff, reduce batch flush frequency during failover so we don't overload the fallback nodes with lots of tiny batches, and slightly increase prefetch threads for the KV store during route.swap.
00:21:00 Arjun: can redwood do those client policy recommendations as a code snippet? we have multiple SDKs in python/go/java.
00:21:10 Daniel: yes i'll post SDK snippets for python/go/java.
00:22:30 Sophie: circling back to audits — priya you wanted explicit fallback events; leah will draft schema.
00:22:40 Priya: yes and also we need an SSO assertion noting who initiated the failover for postmortem.
00:23:05 Leah: i'll include an audit field for operator_id and method.
00:23:55 Daniel: small note: during the last sim one of the fallback nodes hit a kernel oops and rebooted — non-deterministic but likely driver combo. we'll include a checklist to exclude suspect driver versions from fallback pools until patched.
00:24:30 Arjun: can you tag those nodes in the fleet and exclude them from canary?
00:24:38 Daniel: yes we can maintain a tagged exclude-list that the scheduler respects.
00:25:20 Maya: curious if competitors like deepcloud do a similar pre-warm — they claim instant failover but in practice there's warmup.
00:25:30 Sophie: i've heard that too, competitors marketing is slick; reality is usually similar tradeoffs. we'll lean on redwood's fallback/runbook approach.
00:26:10 Jonas: question — do we want to test a partial network partition scenario instead of full egress blackhole? might be closer to real world.
00:26:22 Daniel: agreed, partial partition is good to add to the matrix — we'll simulate packet loss and increased RTT for a subset of subnets. that often surfaces other issues like retransmits.
00:27:05 Arjun: ok let's include a matrix of sims: 10% egress loss, increased RTT 100–200ms, full blackhole, and small GC spikes on nodes.
00:27:30 Sophie: perfect. we'll attach that matrix to the runbook.
00:28:10 Maya: anything else on upgrades? kernel rollback plan, driver pinning, and an exception window for production?
00:28:25 Daniel: yes — propose a maintenance window after rehearsal and before full roll to verify metrics. rollback plan will be in ticket.
00:29:00 Priya: security question — when we do the rehearsal will redwood's control plane require additional access? we have to approve network peering changes during the window.
00:29:10 Leah: we'll send a limited-scope access request and list exact ACL changes; minimal privileges only for the time of the sim.
00:30:00 Sophie: switching gears — can we set target success criteria for the rehearsal?
00:30:12 Daniel: success = p99 under 700ms for 95% of simulated windows, no auth failures, and cache warmup hit rate above 70% within first minute.
00:30:40 Maya: sounds reasonable.
00:31:05 Jonas: i'll make sure on-call is briefed and we have a rollback pager.
00:32:10 Sophie: great. recap quick: daniel to run another sim with priming and a 5% canary, leah to update runbook and audit schema, arjun to enable shadowing and share topology, maya to confirm VIPs and egress, and we schedule rehearsal weeks end of october.
00:32:35 Daniel: i'll also attach the kernel mismatch logs and driver versions in the ticket.
00:33:00 Priya: and redwood please include the certificate chain and handshake timing so we can investigate TLS latency.
00:33:12 Daniel: yep will attach.
00:34:05 Maya: anything on cost controls for priming? we want to cap spend during rehearsal.
00:34:15 Sophie: we can set a priming budget in the job and abort once it crosses threshold, we'll add that to the runbook.
00:35:20 Jonas: question on telemetry endpoints — will traces go into our datadog or will redwood store them?
00:35:30 Leah: we can do both: redwood staging bucket plus stream a subset to your datadog with masked PII.
00:36:10 Arjun: ok that helps compliance.
00:37:00 Daniel: small caveat — for full fidelity tracing we need trace IDs forwarded from your SDK; otherwise correlation is hard.
00:37:20 Jonas: we can add trace id forwarding in SDKs.
00:38:10 Sophie: ok time to call out the explicit next steps and owners — leah will update runbook by monday 10/18, daniel will run sim and attach logs by 10/22, maya/arjun will provide topology and VIP list by 10/19, we target canary week 10/26 and full rehearsal 10/28.
00:39:00 Maya: thanks all — that schedule works for me.
00:39:20 Sophie: any blockers from security?
00:39:30 Priya: just the ACL approval and KMS validation, once we get the access request i'll review fast.
00:40:00 Daniel: i'll include verification steps for KMS and certificate pinning.
00:41:10 Sophie: ok final quick check — competitors or procurement notes?
00:41:20 Maya: procurement asked about price uplift for dedicated fallback pools; we may need an estimate after tests.
00:41:35 Sophie: we'll surface cost delta post-sim.
00:42:10 Daniel: one more observation — our spike correlated with small clients that had aggressive retry loops; we should blacklist or throttle misbehaving SDK versions during failover.
00:42:35 Jonas: i'll run a quick sweep and blacklist old SDKs.
00:43:50 Leah: i'll create the ticket with action items and link the artifacts.
00:44:10 Sophie: thanks everyone, any other Qs?
00:44:20 Maya: none, good session.
00:44:30 Sophie: meeting adjourned, we'll email notes and runbook link. thanks.
